name: binding-price
description: The market of ledger row #13, executed: privacy is bought, binding is not, and here is the equation that makes them one coin. The identity: Tr[|a><a| rho] = (1 + a.r)/2 — every unit of binding slack IS a unit of concealment loss, one-to-one. The flat supply: witnessed over 26 enumerated families AND over a precisely stated continuous family swept exhaustively (2141 parameterized HJW ensembles), the marginal stays I/2 and the reveal stays exactly 1/2 to floating floor. v0.2.0 adds the noise census: under dephasing/damping commit channels the identity survives as an equation of the output marginal (1.7e-16) and the supply survives as flatness by CPTP linearity, while the input-to-output one-to-one bends (dephasing wedge 0.103553 at gamma=1/2) and breaks (damping confiscates gamma/2 of concealment from a perfectly concealed input, minting the matching slack). The two-coin bounded census: per-coin flat at every Schmidt coefficient, the joint reveal movable among perfectly concealing strategies — the honest boundary of the flat supply. The checker enforces the market laws and names counterfeit witnesses; the renderer refuses illegal ledgers.
